tagline.en: The tower above a great square, a carousel and warm bread.
tagline.he: המגדל מעל כיכר גדולה, קרוסלה ולחם חם.

item.en: a bakery window full of baguettes and pastries

success.en: You found me! Want a bite?

placement.support: Hidden shoes on the cobblestones behind the wicker basket of baguettes.
placement.occlusion: The wicker basket of baguettes, drawn back in front of the child from the board, hides her from the waist down; the head, shoulders and chest show above it against the bakery window.
placement.instructions: Paint the child complete and unoccluded, standing at this spot exactly as if the wicker basket of baguettes were not there: the whole head, torso and arms, and the legs down to the feet on the ground. the wicker basket of baguettes is put back in front of the child afterwards from the board itself; do not paint it over the child, and do not paint any part of the child as hidden.

contract.comparators: the girl in the straw hat at the counter and the boy in blue at the basket

targets.action: The child stands on the wooden carousel deck between the poles, watching the horses. Both shoes rest on TOP of the deck and the entire body rises above it. Do not put a head or torso through the deck, under a horse, or in the floor. Use an existing pole only as a narrow natural overlap, never as an excuse to erase the legs.

success.en: You found me! One more ride?

placement.support: Both shoes on the carousel deck behind its front fascia.
placement.occlusion: The carousel fascia, drawn back in front of the child from the board, hides her shoes and shins; the rest of her shows above it among the riders.
placement.instructions: Paint the child complete and unoccluded, standing at this spot exactly as if the carousel's red-and-gold fascia were not there: the whole head, torso and arms, and the legs down to the feet on the ground. the carousel's red-and-gold fascia is put back in front of the child afterwards from the board itself; do not paint it over the child, and do not paint any part of the child as hidden.

contract.comparators: the boy riding the white horse and the children at the carousel's edge

hintText.en: Look at the other side of the carousel.

targets.action: The child stands behind the painter's easel by the café, complete and upright, her head showing above the canvas and her legs between the easel's legs.

item.en: a painter's easel by the café tables
item.he: כן ציור ליד שולחנות בית הקפה

success.en: A little spot in the shade!
You found me! The chairs are tiny.

placement.support: Hidden shoes on the cobblestones behind the easel's legs.
placement.occlusion: The painter's easel, drawn back in front of the child from the board, hides her from the neck down except what shows between its legs; her head shows above the canvas.
placement.instructions: Paint the child complete and unoccluded, standing at this spot exactly as if the painter's easel with its canvas and tripod legs were not there: the whole head, torso and arms, and the legs down to the feet on the ground. the painter's easel with its canvas and tripod legs is put back in front of the child afterwards from the board itself; do not paint it over the child, and do not paint any part of the child as hidden.

contract.comparators: the girl in the blue dress and the boy in orange beside the easel

hintText.en: Look behind the painter's easel by the café tables.
hintText.he: חפשו מאחורי כן הציור ליד שולחנות בית הקפה.

hintText.en: Look at the café on the right.

targets.expression: mischievous and delighted, eyes wide, mid-giggle, as if about to be spotted

artNotes: the Eiffel tower large and complete in the middle of the picture
a wide stone plaza in front of it, full of tiny people
a carousel with painted horses at one edge of the plaza
a bakery window full of baguettes and pastries
artists painting at easels facing the tower
flower boxes on every balcony around the square

completeText.en: You found {name} three times in Paris!

reaction.en: Excuse me, that is a hat!

artComposition: The Eiffel Tower is the subject: draw it LARGE and complete, from its four feet to its tip, standing in the middle of the picture at the far side of a wide open plaza. It should be the first thing anyone sees. The plaza in front of it is full of tiny people, with the carousel, the bakery and the café tables around its edges.
